subject: Remediation timeline and offset proposal for March 7 outage
messages:
From: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@nimbuscare.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: James Kwon <james.kwon@nimbuscare.com>; billing@nimbuscare.com
Date: 2027-03-07T11:40:00Z
Subject: Outage March 7 — impact summary and request for credit estimate

Hi Evelyn,

We experienced a significant disruption of inference traffic for our production endpoints between ~03:28–05:40 UTC on 2027-03-07 (roughly 2h12m). During that window, our health checks show ~100% failure for two key routes and customer-facing latency spiked before full degradation. This affected our chat flow and billing usage reporting for several accounts.

Attached are an export of our internal monitoring (incident-impact-log.csv) and a screenshot from our uptime dashboard (uptime_screenshot.png) that shows the gap. We need: 1) confirmation of Redwood’s view of the incident window, 2) whether this qualifies for an SLA offset under our contract, and 3) a preliminary credit estimate so we can plan our finance reconciliation.

Can you confirm next steps and an estimated timeline for numbers? We’d like to get this settled before our next billing cycle.

Thanks,
Ana Ruiz
Head of Operations, NimbusCare
ana.ruiz@nimbuscare.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@nimbuscare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outage March 7 — impact summary and request for credit estimate

Hi Ana — thanks for the data and the clear timeline. We’ve started a parallel verification on our side.

On Mon, Mar 7, 2027 at 11:40 AM UTC Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@nimbuscare.com> wrote:
> We experienced a significant disruption ...

Preliminary findings (quick summary):
- Redwood observed elevated error rates for the customer-facing inference cluster between 03:26–05:38 UTC. Our logs show repeated health-check failures and a partial cache warm-up failure that amplified token latency.
- Duration we’re using for the preliminary calc: 2 hours 12 minutes = 132 minutes.
- For a 30-day month the total minutes = 43,200. 132 / 43,200 = ~0.3056% downtime for March.
- Contract SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime (allowed downtime ~43.2 minutes / month). The observed downtime exceeds that threshold by ~88.8 minutes (~0.2056% of total minutes).

Preliminary credit approach (per our standard offset matrix in the customer SLA):
- If monthly uptime < 99.9% and >= 99.5%: 10% credit of monthly invoice.
- If monthly uptime < 99.5% and >= 99.0%: 25% credit.
- If monthly uptime < 99.0%: 50% credit.

With the preliminary numbers above, NimbusCare’s March uptime would land in the 99.69% range (prelim), which maps to the first bracket. Our ballpark estimate is a 15% one-time invoice credit (we use a stepped interpolation inside the bracket in practice). That is contingent on final verification of: 1) exact impacted resource set (we’ll correlate request IDs), and 2) no customer-level mitigations that would adjust the eligible window.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll run a log-level reconciliation (Redwood Rt & NimbusCare logs) to lock the exact start/end times — target by EOD Tue (tomorrow).
2) Finance & Legal will review the credit calc; I’ll route a preliminary PDF that explains the math (attached: prelim-credit-estimate.pdf).
3) If agreed, we’ll prepare a one-time invoice credit and share the timeline for when it will appear on your next bill.

I’ve looped in Marissa (billing lead) and Ben (account lead) to coordinate the credit and the finance handoff.

I’ll follow up with the reconciliation outcome tomorrow.

— Evelyn Hart
Account Lead — Enterprise Customers
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Outage March 7 — impact summary and request for credit estimate

Hi Ana — thanks again for the cooperation on log sharing. We completed the reconciliation this morning and have finalized the credit calculation.

Summary of outcome:
- Final verified outage window: 03:26:38–05:38:12 UTC on 2027-03-07 (132 minutes).
- Calculated March monthly uptime for the affected billing metric: ~99.6944%.
- Eligible offset per the contract matrix: interpolated to a 15% one-time invoice credit.
- Final credit amount (per the March invoice submitted to Redwood): $9,750.00.

Planned mechanics and timeline:
- This will be issued as a one-time invoice credit applied to your April billing cycle. It will appear as line item: "One-time SLA credit — March 07 2027 incident (DEAL-9982)".
- Finance will post the credit on 2027-03-20 and it will reflect on the next invoice PDF.
- We will also send a short credit agreement for signature (attached: credit-agreement.pdf) to confirm the amount and that this resolves the SLA claim.

Operational follow-ups:
- Root cause: engineering found a cascading KV-cache eviction during a capacity rebalance that prevented fast failover for a shard. The postmortem doc is available here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1nimbus-postmortem-2027-03-07 (public to the NimbusCare link we shared).
- We’ve scheduled a follow-up call to review the RCA and mitigations on 2027-03-17; I’ll send invites.

If that timeline and the amount work for you, please reply to confirm and we’ll route the credit agreement for signature.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Lead — Enterprise Customers
Redwood Inference
